title: 357. Geometry, Spatial Thinking & Measurement: Arc Length of a Circle
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.learningObjective: Identify the formula for the arc length of a circle given the central angle in degrees.
questions.question: Which formula gives the length \(L\) of an arc of a circle with radius \(r\) and central angle \(\theta\) measured in degrees?
questions.explanation:
The arc length is a fraction of the circumference. Since a full circle has \(360^\circ\) and circumference \(2\pi r\), the arc length is
\[
L=\frac{\theta}{360}\cdot 2\pi r.
\]
Option A uses the area formula \(\pi r^2\), not the circumference.
questions.hint: Recall that arc length is a fraction of the circle’s circumference.

questions.learningObjective: Calculate the arc length given the radius and central angle.
questions.question: A circle has radius \(6\text{ cm}\). What is the length of an arc with central angle \(60^\circ\)?
questions.explanation:
Using the arc length formula,
\[
L=\frac{60}{360}\cdot 2\pi(6)=\frac{1}{6}\cdot 12\pi=2\pi\text{ cm}.
\]
Therefore, the arc length is \(2\pi\text{ cm}\).

questions.learningObjective: Calculate the arc length for a \(90^\circ\) central angle.
questions.question: A circle has radius \(10\text{ cm}\). What is the length of an arc with central angle \(90^\circ\)?
questions.explanation:
Using the arc length formula,
\[
L=\frac{90}{360}\cdot 2\pi(10)=\frac{1}{4}\cdot 20\pi=5\pi\text{ cm}.
\]
Therefore, the arc length is \(5\pi\text{ cm}\).
questions.hint: A \(90^\circ\) angle corresponds to one quarter of the circle.

questions.concept: Finding Central Angle from Arc Length
questions.learningObjective: Determine the central angle given the arc length and radius.
questions.question: An arc of a circle with radius \(12\text{ cm}\) has length \(8\pi\text{ cm}\). What is the measure of its central angle?
questions.explanation:
Using \(L=\frac{\theta}{360}\cdot 2\pi r\),
\[
8\pi=\frac{\theta}{360}\cdot 2\pi(12)=\frac{\theta}{360}\cdot 24\pi.
\]
Dividing both sides by \(24\pi\) gives
\[
\frac{\theta}{360}=\frac{8\pi}{24\pi}=\frac{1}{3}.
\]
Thus \(\theta=120^\circ\).
questions.hint: Set up the arc length formula and solve for \(\theta\).

questions.concept: Finding Central Angle from Arc Length
questions.learningObjective: Determine the central angle from a given arc length and radius.
questions.question: An arc of a circle with radius \(9\text{ cm}\) has length \(15\pi\text{ cm}\). What is the measure of its central angle?
questions.explanation:
Using the arc length formula,
\[
15\pi=\frac{\theta}{360}\cdot 2\pi(9)=\frac{\theta}{360}\cdot 18\pi.
\]
Dividing both sides by \(18\pi\) gives
\[
\frac{\theta}{360}=\frac{15\pi}{18\pi}=\frac{5}{6}.
\]
Thus \(\theta=\frac{5}{6}\cdot 360^\circ=300^\circ\).

questions.learningObjective: Compare arc lengths in the same circle using central angles.
questions.question: In the same circle, arc \(AB\) subtends a central angle of \(72^\circ\), and arc \(CD\) subtends a central angle of \(36^\circ\). Which arc is longer?
questions.explanation: In the same circle, arc length is proportional to the central angle. Since \(72^\circ>36^\circ\), arc \(AB\) subtends a larger central angle and is therefore longer.
questions.hint: Compare the central angles; the larger angle gives the longer arc.

questions.question: A circle has radius \(7\text{ cm}\). What is the length of an arc with central angle \(\frac{\pi}{3}\) radians?
questions.explanation:
When the central angle is in radians, the arc length is
\[
L=r\theta.
\]
Substituting \(r=7\) and \(\theta=\frac{\pi}{3}\) gives
\[
L=7\cdot \frac{\pi}{3}=\frac{7\pi}{3}\text{ cm}.
\]

questions.learningObjective: Determine the radius given the arc length and central angle.
questions.question: An arc of length \(10\pi\text{ cm}\) subtends a central angle of \(120^\circ\). What is the radius of the circle?
questions.explanation:
Using \(L=\frac{\theta}{360}\cdot 2\pi r\),
\[
10\pi=\frac{120}{360}\cdot 2\pi r=\frac{1}{3}\cdot 2\pi r=\frac{2\pi r}{3}.
\]
Multiplying both sides by \(3\) gives \(30\pi=2\pi r\), so \(r=15\text{ cm}\).
questions.hint: Substitute the known values and solve for \(r\).

questions.learningObjective: Determine the central angle in radians from the arc length and radius.
questions.question: An arc of a circle with radius \(8\text{ cm}\) has length \(6\pi\text{ cm}\). What is the measure of its central angle in radians?
questions.explanation:
Using the radian formula \(L=r\theta\),
\[
6\pi=8\theta.
\]
Dividing both sides by \(8\) gives
\[
\theta=\frac{6\pi}{8}=\frac{3\pi}{4}.
\]

questions.learningObjective: Apply arc length to a clock problem.
questions.question: The minute hand of a clock is \(10\text{ cm}\) long. How far does the tip of the minute hand move in \(20\text{ minutes}\)?
questions.explanation:
In \(20\text{ minutes}\), the minute hand rotates through
\[
\frac{20}{60}\cdot 360^\circ=120^\circ.
\]
The tip traces an arc of radius \(10\text{ cm}\). Using
\[
L=\frac{\theta}{360}\cdot 2\pi r,
\]
we get
\[
L=\frac{120}{360}\cdot 2\pi(10)=\frac{1}{3}\cdot 20\pi=\frac{20\pi}{3}\text{ cm}.
\]
Therefore, the tip moves \(\frac{20\pi}{3}\text{ cm}\).
questions.hint: Find the central angle swept in \(20\text{ minutes}\), then use the arc length formula.
